text: The phosphopeptides keep calcium and phosphate dissolved as tiny amorphous particles, which in a paste can top up the enamel surface. Lab-scale conditions from the Reynolds patent; the commercial process may differ.

links.name: Cross, Huq & Reynolds 2007, Curr Pharm Des

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: digest
steps.note: Trypsin, an enzyme, is added at 0.2 % of the casein weight to a 10 % casein solution, with pH held at 8.0 by sodium hydroxide.

steps.name: clarify
steps.note: The solution is acidified to pH 4.6 and what falls out is spun off or membrane-filtered, or it is membrane-filtered at pH 8.0 instead.
The clear liquid is taken to pH 9.0, then calcium chloride (1.6 M) and disodium phosphate (1 M) are added slowly.
